thread.title: Nikkei rises as Kuroda renominated to lead Bank of Japan

author: morningstar.com
title: Nikkei rises as Kuroda renominated to lead Bank of Japan
text:
By Suryatapa Bhattacharya
Most Asian markets closed for Lunar New Year holiday
Stocks in Japan, Australia and New Zealand gained Friday, while a number of major markets were closed for the Lunar New Year holiday, as investors regained confidence in equities after sharp slides last week.
Taking cues from another robust session on Wall Street overnight, Japan's Nikkei Stock Exchange led gains in Asia, rising 1.2%, despite a stronger yen.
And as expected, Gov. Haruhiko Kuroda was nominated to lead the Bank of Japan for a second term.
The markets that are open took their cues from improving investor sentiment this week and gains in global stocks overnight.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished above 25,000 for the first time since Feb. 2, with market participants expressing greater comfort about the prospect of higher U.S. inflation and Treasury yields.
Japanese technology stocks tracked the gains of U.S. counterparts, including Apple (AAPL) , overnight. Kyocera was higher 3.9% and Sony (6758.TO) gained 3%.
Japan's car makers were also higher despite the stronger yen. Honda Motor (HMC) was up 1.9%, Toyota Motor (7203.TO) added 1.2% and Nissan Motor (NSANY) gained 1.1%.
The dollar was trading at Yen106.22 having fallen to Yen106.01 earlier in the morning, its lowest point since November 2016, prompting a response from Japanese Finance Minister Taro Aso.
"Stability of foreign exchange rates is important, and there is no change in the government's stance that it will take appropriate action at the appropriate time, if needed," he said, escalating his language from a day earlier.
In addition to Kuroda's renomination, the Japanese government also nominated Masazumi Wakatabe and Masayoshi Amamiya for deputy governor positions at the central bank. Amamiya is a career BOJ official. Wakatabe is a professor at Waseda University and is viewed as an advocate of radical easing.
"[Market participants] want to see how monetary policy stance is set to change under the new deputies in [Mr.] Kuroda's second term," said Hiroki Shimazu, chief strategist at MCP Inc.
In Australia, the S&P/ASX 200 was up 0.1%, building on yesterday's rebound with broad gains in industrial, health care and bank stocks. The index is on track for a 1.5% rebound this week after tumbling 4.6% last week.
New Zealand's shares were up 0.5%, helped by a strong rise from one of its biggest stocks. Auckland International Airport (AIA.NZ) was about 3% higher after saying its first-half profit was higher while narrowing its earnings guidance for the fiscal year. Friday's gains come despite further losses for Fletcher Building (FBU.NZ) , taking its slide this week to about 11%. The solid gains for the NZX 50 come after the index reached a three-month low earlier in the week.
